title: Largest Rectangle In Histogram
statement: You get the heights of bars in a histogram. Every bar is 1 wide and bars touch. Find the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside the histogram. The rectangle must be built from whole bars next to each other.

example.caption: The best rectangle uses the bars of height 5 and 6. Its height is 5 and its width is 2, so the area is 10.

idea.sentence: A bar's best rectangle stretches until the first shorter bar on each side. A stack of rising bars finds both limits at the moment a shorter bar pops it.

jargon.plain: A row of touching bars. Each bar has a height and the same width of 1.
A stack kept in one order, here rising heights. A shorter bar pops the taller ones first.

compare.bruteLabel: Try every pair of left and right edges

rows.name: Every pair of edges
rows.note: For each left edge extend right, tracking the lowest bar. Simple, but too slow for large input.

rows.name: Monotonic stack
rows.note: Each bar is pushed once and popped once. All the width work happens at the pop.

fast.takeaway: Do not try every rectangle. Each bar owns one candidate, the widest one at its own height, and the stack finds it when the bar leaves.

stages.title: Setup
stages.note: A stack of bar indices with rising heights, and best = 0. A height-0 bar past the end flushes the stack.

stages.title: Shorter bar pops
stages.note: While the new bar is shorter than the bar on top, that top bar can no longer grow to the right. Pop it.

stages.title: Measure the rectangle
stages.note: Left limit is the bar now on top of the stack, or the start. Right limit is just before the new bar. Area is height times width.

stages.title: Push the bar
stages.note: The new bar can still grow right. Push its index. Heights on the stack still rise.

stages.title: Return
stages.note: Every bar has been popped and measured. best is the answer.

edges.title: One bar
edges.why: It has no neighbours. The end marker pops it with width 1.

edges.title: A zero bar
edges.why: The zero is shorter than everything, so it pops all and no rectangle can cross it.

edges.title: Equal heights
edges.why: Equal bars are not popped by each other. The last pop sees the full width. Using < not <= is still correct.

edges.title: Tall and narrow wins
edges.why: Wide is not always bigger. The single bar of 9 beats the 1 x 4 rectangle.

gotchas.text: Width is i - left - 1, where left is the new top of the stack after popping, or -1 if empty. Using i - popped index gives the wrong width.
Forgetting the end flush leaves rising bars on the stack unmeasured. Looping to i == n with a height of 0 fixes that.
Pop in a while loop. One short bar can end the rectangles of many bars at once.
heights[stack.pop()!] reads the height of the bar you popped. Reading heights[stack[stack.length - 1]] after the pop would give the next bar instead.
The built-in max needs Go 1.21 or later. On older versions write the comparison by hand.
stack[len(stack)-1] panics on an empty slice. Always test len(stack) > 0 first, both in the loop condition and when finding left.

recap.key: Keep indices of rising bars. A shorter bar pops the top and measures its rectangle between the new top and itself.
moves: Loop i from 0 to n, with height 0 at i = n
While the new bar is shorter than the top, pop it
Width is i - newTop - 1 (or i when empty). Update best
Push i. Return best at the end
